# Macho Meals — Phase 0 Readiness Report

**Date:** 2026-07-30 (rebuilt after the authorised FG4 replacement)  
**Scope:** the 30 canonical sessions, plus two archived runs (`macho_meals_fg4_run02`, `macho_meals_fg5_run02`) audited for documentation only.  
**Generated by:** `scripts/phase0_macho_meals_readiness_audit.py`  
**Evaluator API calls made:** **none.** Phase 0 touches no evaluator.  
**Generation calls made:** exactly one authorised session, `macho_meals_fg4_run04` (§3.5). No other session was generated.  
**Files modified in `core/`, `prompts/`, `agents/`, human transcripts, codebook, existing session logs:** none. One config was *created* (`configs/experiment/macho_meals_fg4_run04.json`); no existing config was modified.

> **STOP — Mandatory Human Stop 1.** No pipeline is implemented and no paid
> evaluation call is made until the researcher authorises Phase 1 explicitly.

## 0. Frozen production evaluator

**Tier 1 production coding uses `gemini-3.5-flash`** (`EVALUATOR_CONFIGS["gemininext"]`,
key `GEMINI_API_KEY_NEXT`), with **no temperature and no thinking configuration
transmitted**.

> **CORRECTION (2026-07-30).** An earlier version of this report described
> `thinking_level=medium` as the frozen parameter. That was wrong: it is a logging
> label in `EVALUATOR_CONFIGS`, never sent in the request. The effective
> configuration is the model default, explicitly unpinned. See
> `frozen_evaluation_spec.md` §2.1. The evaluator-selection validation ran through
> the same unpinned path, so the 100% Gate-1 result was obtained under the default,
> not under a pinned MEDIUM.

Basis: `docs/findings/2026-07-18_evaluator_model_comparison.md`, verified against
the document — `gemini-2.5-flash` scored **81.8%** worst pairwise Gate-1
agreement, below the **85%** repeatability threshold, and is **disqualified** as
primary evaluator; `gemini-3.5-flash` scored **100%** Gate-1 agreement, 100%
quote verification and 100% code preservation. Both achieved the same
discrimination margin (**+0.111**). Not to be reopened, and not to be silently
substituted with 2.5.

Phase 0 makes no evaluator call, so this selection has no effect on anything in
this report. It is recorded in `canonical_experiment_manifest.json` under
`evaluator_decision` and carries two consequences for later phases:

### 0.1 Effective request configuration — RESOLVED

`EVALUATOR_CONFIGS["gemininext"]` carries `thinking_level: "medium"` with the
inline comment *"model default; logged but not set via API"*. Reading the call
path in `scripts/thematic_coding.py`, a thinking configuration is sent **only**
for 2.5-class models (`if "2.5" in _model: _gen_cfg["thinking_config"] = ...`);
for `gemini-3.5-flash` nothing is sent, and `temperature` is unsupported and
omitted.

**Resolved:** the SDK *can* pin it (`google-genai 2.10.0` exposes
`ThinkingConfig(thinking_level=ThinkingLevel.MEDIUM)`), but the frozen configuration
is recorded as **explicitly unpinned/default**, because the evaluator-selection
validation itself ran through the same unpinned path. Pinning now would run
production under a configuration that was never validated. Cache keys encode the
**effective** request configuration and were regenerated accordingly (35/35). Full
statement in `frozen_evaluation_spec.md` §2.1.

Availability evidence: `analysis/coding_frame/gemini_calls.jsonl` contains 14
successful `gemini-3.5-flash` calls dated 2026-07-18, and `GEMINI_API_KEY_NEXT`
is present in the environment. Live availability is a Phase 4 check; no call was
made here.

### 0.2 No artefact currently on disk is reusable as production-corpus coding

Provenance of every JSON in `analysis/coding_frame/`, read from each file's own
`evaluator` field:

| Artefact | Evaluator | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `validation_stage1_gemininext.json` | **`gemini-3.5-flash`** (thinking config not transmitted; `medium` is a recorded label only) | **Gemini 3.5 validation evidence** — the evaluator-selection gate record, *not* production-corpus coding |
| `validation_stage1.json`, `validation_stage1_gemini25.json` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | pilot/historical |
| `validation_tier1reach_tier2_gemini25.json` | `gemini-2.5-flash` | pilot/historical |
| Tier 2b chain (`tier2b_guide_question_*`, `tier2b_discrimination_control_*`, `tier2b_human_ceiling_*`, `tier2b_cross_section_control.json`) | `gemini-2.5-flash` | pilot/historical |

So it is **not** the case that every thematic artefact was produced with Gemini
2.5 — `validation_stage1_gemininext.json` was produced with the frozen production
evaluator. What it contains, however, is the *validation* run that selected the
evaluator, not coding of the production corpus.

The operative conclusion is unchanged and slightly broader: **no artefact on disk
is reusable as production-corpus coding.** The 2.5 artefacts fail the model-ID
match outright; the 3.5 artefact matches on model but is a validation record
covering different material, so it fails the transcript-hash match. Production
Tier 1 must be coded fresh, and the cache key must include the model config so a
2.5 artefact can never satisfy a 3.5 lookup.

This does not change the Tier 2b verdict, which remains binding: Tier 2b
recall/precision stays retired as fidelity evidence, and the per-section theme
lists stay descriptive-only. One provenance note, recorded without reopening it:
that verdict was itself established with `gemini-2.5-flash`. Its central result
was large and unambiguous — 0.0% recall for same-group/different-question pairs
and 0.0% on 7 of 8 unrelated cross-question pairs, against 41–57% within the same
question — so it is not plausibly an artefact of evaluator repeatability. Noted
for the record only.

## 1. Headline

All 30 canonical sessions are **mechanically complete**: every one parses, reaches
`current_section_index=6`, records 7/7 sections `completed=true`, has
`inject_participant_intro=false`, matches its config roster, and had every roster
member contribute at least one turn. **No run is a HARD_EXCLUSION.**

One finding remains material and is now formally ruled on by the researcher (§4.5):

> **The two experimental conditions were generated by two versions of one narrow
> code path — the handling of an invalid engagement assessment.** Earlier enriched
> pathway: invalid assessment → technical silence. Later demographics-only /
> current pathway: retry once, silence only if the retry also fails. Nothing else
> in the generation architecture differed.
>
> After the authorised FG4 replacement, the canonical corpus is **14 runs on the
> earlier path** (all enriched) and **16 on the current path** (15
> demographics-only + `macho_meals_fg4_run04`). Measured exposure:
> **enriched 56 forced silences in 2,295 engagement assessments (2.44%; 14 of 15
> runs affected, range 1.39%–3.90%); demographics-only 1 in 2,494 (0.04%), with 11
> further faults recovered by retry.**

Replacing `macho_meals_fg4_run02` removed the single worst-exposed run — the
enriched maximum falls from 9.38% to 3.90% and the enriched mean from 2.75% to
2.44% — but does not remove the asymmetry.

Classified `MATERIAL_COMPARABILITY_WARNING`, not `HARD_EXCLUSION`: the runs are
internally valid, and the agreed treatment (§4.5) retains them with recall and
precision as primary descriptive outcomes — F1 is secondary/complementary — and an
implementation caveat on reach and interaction metrics.

## 3. FG5 enriched `run02` — failure evidence, exclusion, and `run04` as replacement

### 3.1 The mechanical gates do NOT show a failure

`macho_meals_fg5_run02` passes every per-session gate: 64 entries, 42 participant
turns, 11,838 words, 7/7 sections completed, `current_section_index=6`,
`inject_participant_intro=false`, roster matched, all four participants
contributed, natural termination, 4 engagement faults (2.56%) — squarely in the
normal enriched range. On the gates alone it is indistinguishable from run01,
run03 and run04. This is exactly the situation the instructions anticipated
("no reconsiderar su inclusión aunque algunos archivos parezcan completos").

### 3.2 The technical evidence is in the launcher log, and it is unique

`output/session_logs/macho_meals_fg5_run02/launcher_stdout.log` contains:

```
[moderator reflection] call/parse failed, skipping this cycle: Connection error.
```

Scanning the launcher logs of **all 30 canonical runs plus run02**, the markers
`Connection error` and `call/parse failed` appear in **exactly one run in the
entire corpus: `macho_meals_fg5_run02`.** No other session lost a cycle.

The consequence is real and not visible in the transcript: a moderator reflection
cycle was skipped entirely, so run02 carries one fewer accumulated
`section_summaries` entry than its peers, and the moderator entered a later
section with less context than in every other run. That is a genuine
generation-time degradation, and it independently corroborates the researcher's
decision rather than merely deferring to it.

### 3.3 Status

- `macho_meals_fg5_run02` is **excluded pre-analytically**, by researcher
  decision, corroborated by the evidence above.
- It remains on disk; **no artefact of it enters metrics, coding, caches or
  summaries.** It appears in `run_readiness_audit.csv` and
  `api_failure_and_fallback_audit.csv` labelled `enriched(ARCHIVED)` and is absent
  from `canonical_experiment_manifest.csv/json`.
- Its replacement is `macho_meals_fg5_run04`.

### 3.4 `run04` clears every gate applied to the other 29

61 entries, 38 participant turns, 10,049 words, 7/7 sections, roster matched, all
four participants contributed, natural termination, no lost cycle. Its engagement
forced-silence rate (2.99%) sits mid-range for enriched. It carries one recovered
moderator Pydantic validation failure and one recovered engagement JSON parse
failure — both within the range seen across the corpus. **`run04` does not fail
materially; no stop-and-escalate is triggered on its account.**

### Retry pathway confirmed present

Verified directly from the log schema, not inferred: `fields_coerced` is emitted
on **101 of 101** engagement calls in run04 and on **0 of 64** in run02.
`fields_coerced` is written on every engagement call by the current code and not
at all by the earlier code, so its presence establishes that run04 executed the
retry path. The pathway was present but never exercised, because no engagement
assessment failed validation.

### Canonical mapping

FG4 enriched: canonical replication **1 → `run01`**, **2 → `run04`**,
**3 → `run03`**. FG5 enriched unchanged: **1 → `run01`**, **2 → `run03`**,
**3 → `run04`**. The canonical corpus remains exactly **30 sessions**.

## 4. MATERIAL FINDING — the conditions ran on different engagement code

### 4.1 What differs

`core/participant_agent.py` now retries a failed engagement assessment once
before falling back to silence. Its own comment records the change:

> "Previously this path returned stay_silent immediately, which silenced a
> participant for a technical fault rather than a modelled choice."

Log evidence that the two batches straddle this change:

| | enriched (15 runs) | demographics-only (15 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| `fields_coerced` key in `api_calls.jsonl` | absent in **all** runs | present on **every** engagement call |
| `first_attempt_error_type` key | absent | present |
| `participant_engagement_assessment_retry` events | **0** across all 15 | 12 across 6 runs |
| first call timestamp | 2026-07-29 07:03 → 19:08 | 2026-07-29 21:18 → 2026-07-30 01:16 |

The demographics-only batch ran entirely after the enriched batch, and only it
exercises the retry path.

### 4.2 Magnitude

Canonical corpus after the FG4 replacement:

| Condition | engagement assessments | first-attempt faults | recovered by retry | **forced silences** | rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| enriched (14 earlier-path + run04) | 2,295 | 56 | 0 | **56** | **2.44%** |
| demographics-only (15 current-path) | 2,494 | 12 | 11 | **1** | **0.04%** |

14 of the 15 enriched runs are affected, range **1.39%–3.90%**; the exception is
`macho_meals_fg4_run04`, the new current-path replicate, at 0.00%. 13 of 15
demographics-only runs have zero. Independently corroborated in the launcher
logs: `defaulting to stay_silent` appears 3–7 times per earlier-path enriched run,
in only one demographics-only run, and **not at all** in run04.

For reference, the pre-replacement figures were 62 forced silences in 2,258
assessments (2.75%), range 1.39%–9.38%.

### 4.3 Why it matters

A forced silence removes a participant's speaking opportunity for a technical
reason. Systematically more of them in one arm biases, at minimum:

- **Tier 1 evidence-constrained participant reach/breadth** — a *primary* outcome;
- participation balance, turn and word share, adjacency, chain depth — the
  structural and interactional secondary outcomes;
- any per-participant denominator.

**The direction of the thematic bias is indeterminate.** Suppressed turns reduce
the enriched arm's opportunity to express codes, which would tend to lower
recall — but they also reduce the opportunity to express codes *absent from the
human transcript*, which would tend to raise precision, and they change which
speaker holds the floor next, which can redirect the discussion arbitrarily. For
recall and precision the net effect cannot be signed a priori. It should not be
described as conservative.

### 4.4 Scope of the difference

The difference between the two code paths was limited to **technical-error
recovery**: what happens when an engagement assessment fails validation. It was
not a change to the generation architecture, the prompts, the guide, the models,
the memory configuration or the moderator logic — those are identical across
conditions.

However, **the downstream thematic effect cannot be known exactly.** A suppressed
turn removes an utterance that would otherwise have entered the transcript and
influenced every subsequent turn; there is no counterfactual transcript to
compare against. It is therefore wrong to state that thematic content is
unaffected. The correct statement is that the *code* difference was narrow and
confined to error recovery, while its *consequence* for thematic content is
unquantifiable from the artefacts alone.

It does not invalidate the runs individually, and it is not grounds for
regenerating anything beyond the single authorised replacement (§4.6).

### 4.5 Researcher decision — recorded treatment

The researcher's ruling, now in force:

- The 14 remaining earlier-path enriched runs are **retained as canonical**.
- **Technical-silence exposure is reported per run** (§2 tables and
  `api_failure_and_fallback_audit.csv`).
- **Recall and precision remain primary descriptive outcomes**; F1 is
  secondary/complementary and never substitutes for them.
- **Reach and interaction metrics are retained with an implementation caveat**
  attached wherever they are reported.
- A diagnostic association between forced-silence rate and outcomes was considered
  and **declined** (spec §9, decision D8). Forced-silence counts are preserved only
  as operational metadata and a documented limitation.
- **No claim will be made that denominator adjustments reconstruct the missing
  counterfactual.** They cannot: the suppressed turns and everything they would
  have caused do not exist in any artefact.

### 4.6 Authorised targeted replacement — FG4 run02

Separately, and **before any thematic or condition outcome was evaluated**, the
researcher archived `macho_meals_fg4_run02` as a technical outlier: 6 forced
silences in 64 engagement assessments = **9.38%**, more than twice the
next-highest enriched rate (3.90%). It was replaced by a newly generated
`macho_meals_fg4_run04` — a new stochastic replicate under current code, not a
repair of run02 — which now holds FG4 enriched canonical replication index 2. See
§3.5. run02's config, transcript, states and logs remain intact on disk.

This removes the most exposed run but does not remove the asymmetry: 14 enriched
runs were still generated on the earlier path.

### 6.1 Embedded guide vs the YAML guide — two distinct claims

These are not the same statement and the earlier report conflated them:

1. **Identical embedded guide across configs.** `guide_in_config_sha256` is
   identical across all 30 canonical configs. This says only that every run
   executed the same guide object.
2. **Semantic equivalence with `configs/guides/macho_meals_plant_based_masculinity_uk.yaml`.**
   Verified separately, section by section, after NFKC normalisation and
   curly-quote/dash/whitespace folding:

| Section | index | label | phase | scripted question | suggested probes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 Introduction and instructions | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 0/0 |
| 1 Opening discussion: male friendship and place | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 0/0 |
| 2 Everyday food decision-making | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 4/4 |
| 3 Gender and food choice | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 3/3 |
| 4 Imagining a plant-based shift | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 2/2 |
| 5 Making plant-based foods more appealing | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 0/0 |
| 6 Closing remarks | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | 0/0 |

**Result: semantic equivalence VERIFIED**, with one structural difference — the
embedded guide carries an additional runtime-derived field, `section_purpose`
(e.g. `"Section 2: Everyday food decision-making"`), absent from the YAML.

A raw-hash comparison is **not** a valid test here and was not used: the two
serialisations differ by construction (YAML vs JSON; YAML block scalars carry
trailing newlines), so the embedded-guide hash `e14999a0…` and the YAML file hash
`3c2dd222…` differ even though the content is equivalent.

### Discrepancies between documentation and disk

1. **`fg5_run02` looks complete on the gates** while the design notes describe it
   as failed. Resolved in §3: the failure is real but lives in the launcher log,
   not in the session artefacts. Recording this so nobody later "discovers" a
   complete-looking run and reopens the decision.
2. **The engagement-code change is undocumented in `CHANGELOG.md`** — no entry for
   2026-07-29 or 2026-07-30. It was found from the log schema and the code comment.
3. **32 experiment configs exist for 30 canonical runs** — the extras are
   `macho_meals_fg5_run02.json` and
   `macho_meals_fg1_run01_presynthesisfix_pilot_2026-07-28.json`, both correctly
   outside the whitelist.
4. **`scripts/assess_session_batch.py` must not be used unmodified** — it
   discovers every directory under the session-log root and would silently pull in
   all 11 excluded directories. Confirmed, not used.
5. **`thematic_coding.py` defaults to the disqualified evaluator.** Module-level
   `_MODEL = "gemini-2.5-flash"` is used whenever `evaluator_cfg` is omitted, and
   `scripts/validate_tier1_reach_tier2.py` defaults to `--evaluator gemini25`. The
   production pipeline must pass `EVALUATOR_CONFIGS["gemininext"]` explicitly on
   every call; relying on any default silently selects the disqualified model.
   Recommend the Phase 3 pipeline refuse to run if the resolved model is not
   `gemini-3.5-flash`. No file has been changed — this is a Phase 3 design
   requirement, recorded here.

## 8. Blockers

One decision-blocker, no technical blockers:

- **The engagement-path asymmetry (§4) needs a researcher decision** before the
  between-condition comparison is run. It is not a defect in any run; it is a
  property of the corpus that changes how a primary outcome (reach) and all
  structural/interaction outcomes may be read.

`macho_meals_fg5_run04` passes cleanly, so **no stop-and-escalate is triggered on
FG5**, and the 5×3×2 design is intact.
